newsitem.title: PERU: Peru congress passes $9.172 bln 1997 govt budget.
newsitem.headline: Peru congress passes $9.172 bln 1997 govt budget.

text.p: The Peruvian Congress approved late on Friday the government's proposed 1997 budget expenditure total of 24.765 billion soles, or $9.172 billion.
The 1997 spending total is nominally higher than this year's 22.263 billion soles budget, but lower in real terms when taking into account the estimated 1996 inflation of about 12 percent.
The budget's estimated average exchange rate for next year is 2.70 soles to the dollar.
The budget commits 18.7 percent of funds next year to debt payment, up from 14.1 percent this year, and 44 percent to social spending, up from 40 percent in 1996.

The budget's key macroeconomic estimations for 1997 include economic growth of five percent, inflation of nine percent, as well as the average exchange rate of 2.70 soles to the dollar, up from 2.58 now, and a $1.6 billion trade deficit.
The government-controlled, single-chamber Congress had until the end of Saturday to approve the budget.
Analysts have welcomed the budget saying it sets a conservative macroeconomic framework, with a tight fiscal line and clear commitment to pay foreign debt.
